圉 is the place Yu, not Woyu. 守尉 is the governor together with the commandant, not an assistant governor.

North of Kaifeng he broke Zhao Ben’s host; for throwing back the enemy and leading the escalade he beheaded one army hou, piled up sixty-eight heads, took twenty-six prisoners, and was raised to ministerial grandee.
趙賁 is Zhao Ben. 候 is an army hou, a scout officer; the graph is not 侯, so he did not slay a marquis.

立帳下 names only the tent. The sentence does not say that the tent was Xiang Yu's.

噲等四人 is four men of whom Kuai is one, not Kuai plus four others.

西丞 is the assistant magistrate of Xi county, not an unnamed western assistant. He was struck north of Baishui.

He stormed Zhao Ben’s positions and reduced Mei, Huaili, Liuzhong, and Xianyang.

韓王信 is Xin, king of the kingdom of Hán (韓), not Han Xin (韓信), the king of Chu already seized at Chen.

韓信 here continues the Dai campaign against 韓王信. 參合 is Canhe, not Shenhe.

The king ennobled Ying as full marquis with the style Marquis of Changwen, his income drawn from Duping hamlet in Du.
昌文侯 is a marquis. Lord of Changwen was the earlier title 昌文君.
West of Yan he broke Duke Zhe’s detachment of Wang Wu, claiming five Loufan generals and a lian yin.
West of Yan he broke the army of Wang Wu, Duke of Zhe, claiming five Loufan generals and a lian yin.
柘公王武 is one man, Wang Wu, Duke of Zhe. Yan is the place west of which he was beaten, not part of the title.
In the third year of Han he drew his income as a columned marquis from Duping hamlet in Du.
In the third year of Han he drew his income as a full marquis from Duping hamlet in Du.
列侯 is a full marquis. Columned marquis is an over-literal rendering.
He hit Boyang, then swept east from Xiapi through Nan tong, Qu lu, and Xu.
He hit Boyang, then swept east from Xiapi through Nantong and Qulü, and Xu.
南僮 and 取慮 are the place names Nantong and Qulü, not two-word phrases.
He campaigned against Han Xin of Dai as far as Mayi, detached a column that pacified six counties north of Loufan, slew Dai’s left general, and broke a Hu horse commander north of Wuquan.
He campaigned against King Xin of Han as far as Mayi, detached a column that pacified six counties north of Loufan, slew Dai’s left general, and broke a Hu horse commander north of Wuquan.
漢王信 is King Xin, attacked at Dai. He is not Han Xin, the king of Chu already seized at Chen.
Between his return from the Bu campaign and the High Emperor’s death he served Emperor Hui and Empress Lü as a columned marquis.
Between his return from the Bu campaign and the High Emperor’s death he served Emperor Hui and Empress Lü as a full marquis.
列侯 is a full marquis, not a columned marquis.
He fought at Anyang and Gangli, at Kaifeng against Zhao Fen, and at Quyu and Yangwu against Yang Xiong, claiming twelve heads and ministerial grandee rank.
He fought at Anyang and Gangli, at Kaifeng against Zhao Ben, and at Quyu and Yangwu against Yang Xiong, claiming twelve heads and ministerial grandee rank.
He ranged Liang, then swung west to crush Xing Shuo south of Zi, personally seizing two of Shuo’s commandants and a dozen marshals while bringing in four thousand six hundred eighty men.

He ranged Liang, then swung west to crush Xing Shuo south of Zi, personally seizing two of Shuo’s commandants and twelve marshals and hou officers while bringing in four thousand six hundred eighty men.
司馬、候十二人 are twelve men who were marshals and hou, scout officers. 候 is not a marquis.
He moved independently into Henei, smashed Zhao Fen at Zhaoge, and took two horse generals with two hundred fifty mounts.
He moved independently into Henei, smashed Zhao Ben at Zhaoge, and took two horse generals with two hundred fifty mounts.
趙賁 is Zhao Ben. The English reading Fen is the wrong pronunciation of 賁.
On his own he broke a Zhao army, capturing two marshals, four marquises, and twenty-four hundred men.
On his own he broke a Zhao army, capturing two marshals, four hou officers, and twenty-four hundred men.
候 is an army hou, not a marquis (侯). The English turns four officers into four marquises.
He seized Pingyang, cut down the assistant governor with his own blade while his men slew a garrison commandant, then forced Ye to yield.
He seized Pingyang, cut down the acting chancellor with his own blade while his men slew a garrison commandant, then forced Ye to yield.
守相 is the acting chancellor, not an assistant governor.
As chief of cavalry he campaigned in Dai, struck Han Xin beneath Pingcheng, then drew the host back to Dongyuan.
As chief of cavalry he campaigned in Dai, struck King Xin of Han beneath Pingcheng, then drew the host back to Dongyuan.
At Dai and Pingcheng, 韓信 is King Xin of Han. The previous sentence has already used King Xin of Chu for the other man.

In sum he claimed ninety heads and one hundred forty-two prisoners, broke fourteen armies on his own, took fifty-nine towns, set one commandery and one kingdom and twenty-three counties to rights, captured a king and a pillar-of-state, and thirty-nine officers from two thousand piculs down to five hundred piculs.

In sum he claimed ninety heads and one hundred forty-two prisoners, broke fourteen armies on his own, took fifty-nine towns, set one commandery and one kingdom and twenty-three counties to rights, captured a king and a pillar-of-state, and thirty-nine officers from two thousand piculs down to five piculs.
五石 is five piculs. The English adds a hundred that is not in the Chinese.
